### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, touching **8** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3cb8553c946905bf216dfaa6b84870380d112e25` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b3289e424a6b817c4f05a9dca104d99dedbb5c2d` — the merge of head `47b1c37574444ec65bc0a544281952f2d5ff26af` into base `3cb8553c946905bf216dfaa6b84870380d112e25`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b3289e424a6b817c4f05a9dca104d99dedbb5c2d && git checkout b3289e424a6b817c4f05a9dca104d99dedbb5c2d
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 3cb8553c946905bf216dfaa6b84870380d112e25 47b1c37574444ec65bc0a544281952f2d5ff26af && git checkout -B drift-repro 3cb8553c946905bf216dfaa6b84870380d112e25 && git merge --no-ff 47b1c37574444ec65bc0a544281952f2d5ff26af

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3cb8553c946905bf216dfaa6b84870380d112e25
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 3cb8553c946905bf216dfaa6b84870380d112e25` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

### ① Derived judgments

**1. The order's semantics, per read face (bundle types only, `email_template` today).** Judged on the diff plus the cited code; each face names the case table: base's own member / pair override / pair-added member / dependent-added member / pair and dependent at one member.

- **Env-wide list** (`readFlattenedMetaItems`, `servedOverride && !packageId`): the sole-shipper narrowing now keeps an item bound to another package when `isBundle && baseServesBundleMember(...)`. The base's own member (bound = sole shipper) and the pair's declared override (seated in the base's slot, stamped as the base's) take the unchanged `return true`; the pair's added member (bound PAIR, base does not ship the member) is kept; a dependent's member (bound DEPENDENT) is dropped; a pair's undeclared row at a member the base ships stays dropped. Pair-beside-dependent: the stored rows reach this list from `sys_metadata` per `(slot, package)` (not from the registry's one bare slot), so both are present and the member-grain filter keeps the pair's and drops the dependent's. **Correct.**
- **`?package=BASE` list**: the pair's rows enter as `overrideStandIns`; an undeclared one was recorded in `unseated` and dropped. The new block deletes from `unseated` the pair's row of a name the base ships (`shipsBundleName`) at a member the base does not ship (`baseServesBundleMember`), stamped with the pair's id. A dependent's row never enters a base-scoped read (`readActiveOverlayRows(request)` is scoped to BASE; `overrideRows` are the pair's only). **Correct.**
- **Base-named by-name read** (`readMetaItem`, `request.packageId = BASE`): step 1's served-row candidates (declared override, own row, package-less) are unchanged; the new 1b reads the pair's own row at the wanted member only when `pairOfAddedMember` says the base ships the name and not that member; the registry tier is then guarded by `registryMemberServedAt`. Base's own member: step 1 or the artifact. Pair override: step 1 (`overrideOf`), stamped as the base's. Pair-added member: 1b, stamped PAIR (as the registry tier stamped it before, so the stamp is unchanged). Dependent-added member: 1b finds no pair row; the registry's bare slot holds the dependent's hydrated row; the guard drops it (bound DEPENDENT, base does not serve) → 404. **Correct.**
- **Package-less by-name read**: `contentPackageId` = `packagelessContentPackage` = the one code package that ships the name (BASE) whether the stored rows are bound to PAIR, to DEPENDENT or to both (candidates ≠ 1 ⇒ `null` ⇒ `shippers.size === 1` ⇒ BASE), so 1b and the guard run exactly as on the base-named read. When several packages ship the name and a row is bound to one, `contentPackageId` is `undefined` and nothing changes. **Correct.**
- **`?package=DEPENDENT`** (list and by-name): the list reads the dependent's own rows; its `pairOfList` (`DEPENDENT.custom`) has no rows. By-name: step 1 serves the dependent's own row; `registryMemberServedAt` returns `item` unchanged because the dependent ships no bundle of that name. **Unchanged, as ordered.**
- **`?package=PAIR`**: `customizationPackageId(PAIR)` is not `ok`, so neither new list block runs; by-name step 1 serves the pair's own row. **Unchanged, as ordered.**
- **`getMetaItemsForExecution`**: `readFlattenedMetaItems(..., 'execution')` with `layer: 'effective'` ⇒ `servedOverride` true and no `packageId` ⇒ the env-wide member-grain narrowing applies. **Correct.**
- **`renderTemplate` / `sendTemplate`**: `packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/template-loader.ts:142` reads `getMetaItemsForExecution({ type: 'email_template' })`; a listed pair-added `fr-FR` renders, a dependent's falls to the base's `en-US`. **Correct.**
- **The third change (pair's stored row on the by-name path) — correct, and minimal where it is needed.** Verified in the cited code: the hydrator calls `registry.registerItem(type, registered, 'name')` with NO `packageId`, so every stored row hydrates into the one bare slot `name@member` of `getItem`'s `bare` tier; with a pair row and a dependent row at one member the registry holds one entry, whichever hydrated last. The registry guard alone would therefore answer the dependent's body or nothing, depending on hydration order; reading the pair's own stored row before the registry tier is the only deterministic answer on the by-name face. It is not needed on the list faces, which never consult the registry for stored rows (the overlay merge reads `sys_metadata` per `(slot, package)`), and the dev did not add it there. The A3 ablation reddening only the pair-beside-dependent cases is consistent with this reading.
- **No-member read** (`member` undefined, `wantedMember` = canonical): for a bundle with no canonical member the guard asks the registry for the base's own member (`itemDiscriminator` of the base's artifact) instead of a dependent's canonical one; a bundle that ships the canonical member is unchanged (`pairOfAddedMember` returns `undefined`, the registry answers the base's). The unit test's fourth case pins it. **Correct.**

**2. Bundle-type derivation.** Every new branch is gated on `ITEM_KEY_DISCRIMINATORS[request.type] !== undefined` (scoped list), `isBundle` from the same table (env-wide list), or `wantedMember !== undefined` (`bundleMemberDiscriminator` returns `undefined` for a type with no table entry). No `'email_template'` literal in the diff. For a non-bundle type the env-wide expression reduces to the old `soleShipper === undefined || soleShipper === bound` (`isBundle && …` is `false`), the scoped-list block is skipped, and neither by-name addition runs. **Byte-identical behaviour for non-bundle types by construction**; the control is the package suites (metadata-protocol 296 files, objectql 520 files) and the full dogfood battery, not a dedicated non-bundle case — see should-fix ③ S1.

**3. Write gate.** The diff touches neither `protocol-packaged-base-refusal.ts` nor `packaged-base-regime.ts` (PR #28777's files, merge `5bb7834a` is an ancestor of this head). The dogfood keeps the `403 NOT_OVERRIDABLE` control for a dependent's `en-US`. **Untouched, as ordered.**

**4. Evidence.**
- Red first: dogfood on main `c064d3a2` 4 failed / 6 passed (the four behaviour cases), green 10/10 at the head under the lock; the new objectql unit 5/5 red on the base's `metadata-protocol` source, 5/5 green at the head. Consistent with the diff's four behaviour changes.
- Ablations: A1 (member-grain list change) reds the pair-addition cases only, A2 (registry guard) the dependent cases only, A3 (pair stored-row read) the pair-beside-dependent case only; each leg via `ablation-replace.mjs` with `dist/` preflight `--absent`, restore verified to the head blob; the first A1 attempt that failed the DTS build is reported as measuring nothing. As reported; not re-run here. **Accepted.**
- PR #28800's pin flipped: the SHAPE cases are renamed to the behaviour and assert the 404; a second describe (own boot) pins the pair addition and the pair-plus-dependent case; the file header no longer says "does not assert the shape is right". **Done.**
- Controls present: the base's own `en-US` on every read, the pair's declared `en-US` override (stamped as the base's), `?package=PAIR` unchanged, the dependent's `en-US` refusal. Absent: an explicit non-bundle type list control (S1).
- Gates: the local sweep file records 66 families, all exit 0 (one prerequisite re-run). Check-runs on the head at read time: 23 success, 13 skipped, 11 in progress, 0 failures (`Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates` success; Type Check, ESLint, Build Core, Test Core 1–8, Live E2E UI in progress). The dogfood shards are skipped on the PR run, so the flipped dogfood file first runs in CI in the merge group; the dev ran it and the full battery locally under the lock.
- Overlap: open #28811, #28808, #28731 touch `protocol.ts` (and #28811 `registry.ts`); their patches do not touch `soleShippingPackage`, the stand-in set's deletion, `findServedOverlayRow`, `registry.getItem` or `ITEM_KEY_DISCRIMINATORS` (#28811 renames the slot-name read inside `mergePackageAwareOverlay`, a different seam). #28791 is merged on main (`registry.ts` only). `git merge-tree` of the head against current `origin/main` (`3e05ed1e`) is clean.

**5. Skills-docs.** The PR body carries `Skills-docs: follow-up owed — skills/objectstack-platform/SKILL.md, content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`. Under pm-dispatch SKILL.md (the `Metadata-protocol` line's third-line rule) `follow-up owed — FILES` is a legal value and the seat files the owed card and rewrites it to `follow-up #N` before ACCEPT; the review checklist makes the missing rewrite a REWORK. So a follow-up is enough under the repo rules; the rewrite is owed by the seat (③ S2). Open #28778 / PR #28814 already edits exactly these two files and is the natural carrier.

### ② Semver level

- **Clause-②: `yes (narrowing)` — correct.** Widening: a pair-added member of a bundle is served on the base's address (lists, execution list, by-name reads, send). Narrowing: a by-name read naming the base or no package no longer answers a member the base's address does not own through the registry's cross-package tier (`200` → `404`). The widening is stated in the PR body and changeset prose; the title carries `!`; the BREAKING banner and the ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker are in the changeset body.
- **Metadata-protocol: `semantic` — correct; the claim's expected `narrowed` is not.** AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3 defines the line as the change to what a metadata author can write: `narrowed` = a key removed or tombstoned, a value refused or a requirement tightened; `semantic` = a changed meaning or default. Nothing an author writes is refused here — the #28746/#28777 write gate is untouched, a dependent's locale under a base name is still accepted and still served under its own package. What changed is the meaning of a written locale on the base's address: a pair-added locale now means "listed and sent for the base"; a dependent's means "the dependent's own, served under its package only". That is `semantic`; the breaking read-side narrowing is carried by the `(narrowing)` arm, the banner and the ADR-0087 marker, which is exactly how `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` separates the two (`narrowed` must sit beside a `(narrowing)` arm; `semantic` beside one is not a contradiction). Open question answered: **option A, accept `semantic`.**
- **Changeset level: `@objectstack/metadata-protocol: minor` — satisfied under either arm.** The level follows the kind alone: `narrowed` and `semantic` each take at least `minor` on a package the diff moves (`protocol.ts`, `protocol-environment-rows.ts` are its published source); `none` would take `patch`. The gate's level axis therefore demands `minor` whichever kind is declared; the committed changeset declares `minor`, the local sweep records `check-changeset-no-major.mjs --base origin/main :: exit 0`, and the head's `Check Changeset` check-run concluded success. Both declaration lines are in the PR body and the changeset body, line-initial.
- Dogfood battery owed by the `(narrowing)` arm: reported run at the head under the lock, no shard, no path — Test Files 380 passed, 3 skipped; Tests 3118 passed, 28 skipped; VERDICT exit 0. As reported.

### ③ Boundary flags

Author `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no relay login to name.

- **Open question (Metadata-protocol kind): answered above — `semantic`.** No change to the PR.
- **S1 (should-fix): no explicit non-bundle control.** The order's control list named "a non-bundle type's lists byte-identical"; the diff's gating makes it true by construction and the suites cover it, but no case in either new test file lists a non-bundle type beside the bundle cases. Acceptable as is; a one-case control in `protocol-bundle-member-base-address.test.ts` would make the ablation legs prove it.
- **S2 (seat, before ACCEPT): rewrite `Skills-docs:` to `follow-up #N`** — fold into #28778 / PR #28814 (which already edits both files) or file a card; the body currently reads `owed — FILES`.
- **S3 (should-fix, prose): the narrowed set is wider than "a dependent's".** `registryMemberServedAt` drops ANY other package's member the registry's first-match tier answered on a base's address — a dependent's, and a same-named package outside the closure (ADR-0048 §3.3 coexistence on a bare name; ADR-0146 D8 item 2 says such an item is not a candidate for the base's address at all, so the behaviour is right). The changeset's "Narrowed" bullet names only the dependent; say "another package's" so the CHANGELOG reader is not surprised.
- **Dormant, noted by the dev, agreed:** `previewDrafts` of a pair-added member on the base's address falls through to the active read (serves the pair's published row); a package-unbound row at the same unshipped member is served first by the by-name read while the scoped list's stand-in is the unbound row (pre-existing ordering). Neither is reached by a documented door today.
- **Flag (follow-up card owed, not this PR): the layered read.** `/layers?package=BASE&member=fr-FR` still answers 404 for a pair-added member (noted on PR #28800 and here). ADR-0146 D8 lists the layered read among the five that must agree; the order's face list did not include it. The seat should file it as a D8 card.
- **Flag (not measured): the `version` token** the base-named read returns for a pair-added member (the lock is selected from the read's address, where no base row exists). No door edits a pair-added member through the base's address, so dormant; worth one line in the D8 card above.

### ① Derived judgments

- **S1 folded (non-bundle control) — accepted.** The new case lays a pair's and a dependent's `view` row under a name the base ships (the write gate stubbed for the seeding, rows the gate refuses today), then asserts: the per-package layer carries all three bodies (`['status', 'title', 'title,status']`); the env-wide list and the list scoped to the base keep the base's item alone (`[[BASE, ['title','status']]]`); the bundle's env-wide members beside it are untouched. That is exactly the name-grain rule the diff leaves in place for a type with no `ITEM_KEY_DISCRIMINATORS` entry: the env-wide filter's new arm is `isBundle && …`, false for `view`, and the scoped-list block is gated on the table. Reported A1 (drop the member-grain list change): the control stays green and only the three pair-addition cases go red — consistent with the control exercising the unchanged branch. The control reads `getMetaItemsPerPackage`, `getMetaItems` and `getMetaItems({ packageId })`; the by-name face has no non-bundle case, which is fine: both by-name additions are gated on `wantedMember !== undefined`, `undefined` for every non-bundle type.

Declaration lines, BREAKING banner and the ADR-0087 marker are unchanged.
- **S2 done by the seat.** The PR body's third line reads `Skills-docs: follow-up #28829` (open: a docs/skills card naming SKILL.md and metadata-lifecycle.mdx for this behaviour). The layered-read gap is filed as #28830 (open, ADR-0146 D8). Both cards read as owed and correctly scoped.
- **Side reading (not filed): the per-package layer stamps the pair's and the dependent's view bodies with the base's `_packageId`.** Judged on the head's code, cited above:
  - *Mechanism.* `getMetaItemsPerPackage` is `readFlattenedMetaItems(..., 'served', 'per-package')`, `servedOverride` false. The overlay merge seats each package-bound row in its own `(slot, package)` and stamps a body with no `_packageId` as its own package (`_packageId: real`), so after the merge the rows read PAIR and DEPENDENT. The stamp changes at the envelope graft at the end of the list read (`protocol.ts` around 10681–10684, #22024): `itemPackageId = envelopePackageId(undefined, it)` is the item's own package, and `lookupArtifactItem('view', name, PAIR)` → `registry.getArtifactItem` → prefer-local (no PAIR artifact) → **the first composite entry of a genuine code package** (`registry.ts` 6749–6753) → the base's view artifact; `mergeArtifactProtection` then sets `out._packageId = a._packageId` = BASE (`protocol.ts` 2538). The #22024 scoping ("graft each item's own provenance envelope, not the first-registered package's") is defeated by the artifact lookup's cross-package fallback for a package that ships no artifact of the name.
  - *Pre-existing and out of scope: yes.* None of these lines is in the #28802 diff (the diff touches the sole-shipper filter, the scoped list's stand-in set, the by-name read's pair row and registry guard); the per-package layer runs none of the new blocks (every one is gated on `servedOverride`, on the key table, or on `wantedMember`); the graft and `getArtifactItem`'s fallback predate the merge-base. On the served faces the order governs, such a row is dropped (env-wide, base-scoped) or served under its own address, so the stamp never reaches an ordered face. The control asserts columns, not stamps, on the per-package layer, so it does not pin the mis-stamp as right.
  - *Deserves a card: yes, low priority (p3), not this PR.* The per-package layer is read by `packages/rest/src/form-routes.ts:256` (the anonymous form doors' withdrawal layer, views) and `packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts:3311` (the package export). A row another package stored under a base's name wears the base's provenance there — a read that names the wrong author of a body, and the export is a provenance carrier (ADR-0146 D8 item 3). Reach today: an undeclared pair row or a dependent's row under a base's name is refused at publish since #28364 / PR #28777's family, so only legacy stored rows (the D11 migration's input) can reach it, and the control had to stub the gate to seed them. Also worth one line on the card: the same fallback can stamp a pair's row in the pair's own scoped export (`packageId: PAIR` requested) with the base's id, which is intended for a declared override and not measured for anything else.
